FINDING_ID: Codex_R2_LB_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.89  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.79  
DESCRIPTION: At [dynamic_management.py:907](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L907), [dynamic_management.py:919](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L919), and [dynamic_management.py:936](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L936), the greedy solver orders only by criticality, then greedily balances small tasks before large ones, and finally force-assigns on failure. That can create an F1 violation even when a feasible allocation exists. Direct execution with two `PAR` models of capacity 10 and tasks `(1, 1, 1, 10)` produced `[[1,0],[0,1],[1,0],[0,1]]`, overloading `m2` to 11, even though `(0,0,0,1)` is feasible with loads `[3,10]`. This is not just “solver may return infeasible”; the heuristic itself manufactures infeasibility from a feasible instance.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Before force-assignment, run a small exact/backtracking feasibility repair on the remaining task set, or at minimum sort by `(criticality desc, token_demand desc)` and use a best-fit heuristic instead of pure least-loaded placement.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R2_LB_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.85  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.82  
DESCRIPTION: The class advertises a multi-objective cost `J(A)` at [dynamic_management.py:794](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L794), but `_solve_greedy()` never uses `c`, `tau`, `lambda_lat`, or `lambda_bal` when choosing a model; it sorts only by current load fraction at [dynamic_management.py:919](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L919). In direct execution with `lambda_lat=1000`, one `slow_expensive` model (`tau=1000`, `c=100`) and one `fast_cheap` model (`tau=1`, `c=1`), the solver assigned the task to whichever model appeared first in the input list. The objective for assigning the slow model was `101000.0`; the objective for the fast model was `110.0`. So the implementation is input-order dependent where the stated objective has a 900x preference.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Rank candidate models by incremental objective delta `ΔJ` for the proposed assignment, not just load fraction; use load fraction only as a secondary tie-breaker.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R2_LB_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.80  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71  
DESCRIPTION: `_objective()` and `_balanced()` map any `L <= 0` model to load fraction `0.0` via `np.where(limits > 0, loads / limits, 0.0)` at [dynamic_management.py:818](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L818) and [dynamic_management.py:879](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L879). That masks catastrophic overload in the very metrics returned to callers. Direct execution with two zero-limit models and one 10-token task returned `cost 10.0` and `balanced True` despite an F1 violation. This also contradicts [dynamic_management.py:713](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L713), where `Allocation.model_load_fraction()` correctly treats positive load on `L <= 0` as `inf`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Treat positive load on nonpositive-capacity models as `inf` in both objective and balance calculations, or reject `L <= 0` at construction time.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R2_LB_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.76  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74  
DESCRIPTION: The allocation API never enforces unique `model_id` or `task_id`, and the lookup methods silently corrupt results when duplicates exist. `Allocation.get_assigned_tasks()` and `get_assigned_models()` use `list.index()` at [dynamic_management.py:687](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L687) and [dynamic_management.py:678](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L678), so duplicate IDs alias to the first row/column only. `model_load()` collapses tasks into a dict at [dynamic_management.py:699](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L699), so duplicate task IDs overwrite each other. Direct execution with duplicate model IDs `['dup','dup']` produced a two-column matrix but `get_assigned_tasks('dup')` returned only the first column’s tasks. With duplicate task IDs, `model_load()` returned `198.0` for two tasks of 10 and 99 because both rows were charged at the later task’s demand.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add `__post_init__` validation on `Allocation`, `Task`, and model/task inputs to reject duplicate IDs and matrix-shape mismatches before any lookup occurs.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R2_LB_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.72  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.68  
DESCRIPTION: `LoadBalancer` never validates that `role_map` covers exactly the active model set. In `_admissibility_mask()`, missing entries default to `Role.PAR` at [dynamic_management.py:771](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L771), and `k_total` is computed from whatever happens to be in `role_map` at [dynamic_management.py:767](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L767). Direct execution with models `['missing_role', 'pm']` and `role_map={'pm': Role.PM}` produced mask `[[1,1]]`; when `missing_role` was listed first, it was assigned the task despite never receiving a role. That is fail-open behaviour at a role-gated boundary.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate in `__init__` that `set(role_map.keys()) == set(model.model_id for model in models)` and raise on any missing or extra role entries; do not default missing models to `PAR`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R2_LB_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.67  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.60  
DESCRIPTION: `ModelSpec` and `Task` define numeric invariants in prose but enforce none at [dynamic_management.py:304](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L304) and [dynamic_management.py:323](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L323). As a result, negative `token_demand` flows straight into load and cost calculations at [dynamic_management.py:807](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L807) and the admission check at [dynamic_management.py:931](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L931). Direct execution with `Task('tneg', -10, ...)` returned `matrix [[1]]`, `model_load -10.0`, and total `cost -13.0`. That creates physically impossible “negative load” allocations and can invert objective comparisons.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add `__post_init__` validation for `Task.token_demand >= 0`, `Task.criticality in [0,1]`, `ModelSpec.L > 0` or `>= 0` by policy, `ModelSpec.tau >= 0`, `ModelSpec.c >= 0`, and `ModelSpec.L_std >= 0`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
